in Fort Worth, Texas, to meet growing demand from data center projects.
The company said the new plant is strategically located to improve proximity to key customers, shorten delivery distances for certain products, and enhance its ability to serve core end markets.
Once the initial production phase begins—anticipated in Q4 2027—Hammond Power

said it expects the facility to add ~C$250M (US$178M) in annual manufacturing capacity, based on anticipated demand, adding that it expects to spend C$50M to equip and commission the initial production phase.
Analysts at National Bank Financial said Hammond Power's
expansion is a "clear positive” since it addresses its emerging capacity constraint while positioning the company to better serve U.S. customers and gain market share.
"This new investment in a U.S. facility is about being closer to our customers and better positioned to support the long-term demand we are seeing for our products," Hammond Power
CEO Adrian Thomas said, adding that demand for transformers continues to increase, particularly from large projects tied to data centers, electrification, and power infrastructure.

title: Hammond Power surges on U.S. expansion plan to meet data center demand
